Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
Work modulo \(397\). Since \(397\) is prime, every nonzero residue has a multiplicative inverse.

First note that none of \(a_0,a_1,\dots,a_{2026}\) can be \(0\): if \(a_k=0\), then the recurrence forces \(a_{k+1}=0\), and hence \(a_{2026}=0\), contradicting \(a_{2026}=9\). Also \(a_{2027}\neq 0\).

Define
\[
b_n \equiv a_n^{-1} \pmod{397}.
\]
From
\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2 \equiv a_n,
\]
take reciprocals:
\[
b_{n+1}\equiv (a_n+1)^2 a_n^{-1}
= a_n+2+a_n^{-1}
= b_n+2+a_n.
\]
Thus
\[
a_n \equiv b_{n+1}-b_n-2.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\),
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n
\equiv \sum_{n=0}^{2026}(b_{n+1}-b_n-2)
= b_{2027}-b_0-2\cdot 2027.
\]
Since \(a_0=1\), we have \(b_0=1\), so
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n \equiv b_{2027}-4055.
\]

Now \(a_{2026}=9\), so
\[
b_{2026}\equiv 9^{-1}.
\]
Because \(9\cdot 44=396\equiv -1\pmod{397}\),
\[
9^{-1}\equiv -44\equiv 353.
\]
Therefore
\[
b_{2027}\equiv b_{2026}+2+9=353+11=364.
\]
Hence
\[
\sum_{n=0}^{2026} a_n \equiv 364-4055.
\]
Since \(4055\equiv 85\pmod{397}\),
\[
364-4055\equiv 364-85=279\pmod{397}.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
